course.title: N5 Foundations
course.description: A practical first path through introductions, study, time, and daily routines.

chapters.title: First steps
chapters.description: Introduce yourself, name familiar things, and ask simple questions.

lessons.title: Meeting people
lessons.subtitle: はじめまして
lessons.description: Build a small introduction you can actually use.

lessons.title: The morning route
lessons.subtitle: 朝の道
lessons.description: Talk about time, places, transport, and what you do each day.

chapters.title: Daily life
chapters.description: Move from naming things to describing simple routines.

lessons.title: Food and routines
lessons.subtitle: 毎日のこと
lessons.description: Use polite verbs and familiar words to describe your day.

lessons.title: Weather and small errands
lessons.subtitle: 雨の日
lessons.description: Talk about the weather, say what you want, and handle a simple purchase.

chapters.title: Everyday world
chapters.description: Point things out, describe places, and ask for simple directions.

lessons.title: Home and directions
lessons.subtitle: 部屋と道
lessons.description: Use object, location, and possession patterns to describe the world around you.

lessons.title: Plans and descriptions
lessons.subtitle: 週末の予定
lessons.description: Describe things, connect actions, and say what you want to do next.

vocabulary.title: 私
vocabulary.notes: In ordinary polite conversation, 私 is a safe default for 'I'.

vocabulary.title: 学生
vocabulary.notes: 学生 can refer to a student generally; 大学生 is specifically a university student.

vocabulary.title: 先生
vocabulary.notes: 先生 is also an honorific for some professionals, but this module uses the teacher meaning.

vocabulary.title: 大学
vocabulary.notes: 大学 can mean both the institution and the campus depending on context.

vocabulary.title: 友達

exampleSentences.translation: I go to the station with a friend.

vocabulary.notes: と marks the person you do something with in the example.

vocabulary.title: 家族

exampleSentences.translation: There are four people in my family.

vocabulary.notes: Use 人数 counters when saying how many people are in a family.

vocabulary.title: 毎日

exampleSentences.japanese: 毎日、日本語を勉強します。

vocabulary.notes: Time words like 毎日 usually do not need に when they describe a recurring action.

vocabulary.title: 朝

exampleSentences.japanese: 朝、コーヒーを飲みます。
exampleSentences.translation: I drink coffee in the morning.

vocabulary.notes: 朝 can be a time setting without に in a natural routine sentence.

vocabulary.title: 駅

exampleSentences.translation: I wait for a friend at the station.

vocabulary.notes: で marks the place where the action of waiting happens.

vocabulary.title: 電車

exampleSentences.japanese: 電車で大学へ行きます。
exampleSentences.translation: I go to university by train.

vocabulary.notes: で can mark the means of transport: 電車で means 'by train'.

vocabulary.title: 家

exampleSentences.translation: I read a book at home.

vocabulary.notes: 家 can mean the building or home as a place, depending on the sentence.

vocabulary.title: 学校

exampleSentences.translation: The school is near the station.

vocabulary.notes: The small っ in がっこう creates a brief pause before こ.

vocabulary.title: 本
vocabulary.notes: 本 also appears in the counter for long cylindrical objects; this lesson uses the noun 'book'.

vocabulary.title: 水
vocabulary.notes: 水 is the ordinary word for water; お水 is a polite service expression.

vocabulary.title: ご飯
vocabulary.notes: In daily speech, ご飯 often means a meal, not only rice.

vocabulary.title: 食べる
vocabulary.notes: The polite form introduced here is 食べます; the dictionary form is 食べる.

vocabulary.title: 飲む

exampleSentences.translation: I drink water at the station.

vocabulary.notes: 飲む is a godan verb; its polite form is 飲みます.

vocabulary.title: 行く

exampleSentences.translation: I will go to university tomorrow.

vocabulary.notes: へ highlights direction; に can also mark a destination.

vocabulary.title: 来る

exampleSentences.translation: A friend comes to my home.

vocabulary.notes: 来る is irregular; its polite form is 来ます（きます）.

vocabulary.title: 見る
vocabulary.notes: Context decides whether 見る is best translated as see, watch, or look at.

vocabulary.title: 勉強する

exampleSentences.japanese: 毎日、日本語を勉強します。

vocabulary.notes: する turns the noun 勉強 into the verb 'to study'.

vocabulary.title: 買う

exampleSentences.translation: I buy a book at the station.

vocabulary.notes: 買う changes to 買います in the polite present form.

vocabulary.title: 大きい
vocabulary.notes: As an い-adjective, 大きい can directly modify a noun.

vocabulary.title: 新しい
vocabulary.notes: The い remains before a noun: 新しい本.

vocabulary.title: 今日

exampleSentences.japanese: 今日は学校へ行きます。
exampleSentences.translation: I am going to school today.

vocabulary.notes: 今日 is commonly read きょう in everyday speech.

vocabulary.title: 明日

exampleSentences.translation: I will go to university tomorrow.

vocabulary.notes: 明日 is a time word and usually does not need に.

vocabulary.title: 月曜日

exampleSentences.japanese: 月曜日に日本語を勉強します。

vocabulary.notes: 曜日 names end in 曜日; the first kanji identifies the day.

vocabulary.title: 天気

exampleSentences.japanese: 今日の天気はいいです。

vocabulary.notes: 天気 is often paired with いい or 悪い when describing conditions.

vocabulary.title: 雨
vocabulary.notes: The noun 雨 can be used with です for a simple weather statement.

vocabulary.title: 傘

exampleSentences.japanese: 雨の日は傘を使います。
exampleSentences.translation: I use an umbrella on rainy days.

vocabulary.notes: 傘 is a practical object for weather conversations and errands.

vocabulary.title: コンビニ

exampleSentences.japanese: コンビニで水を買います。
exampleSentences.translation: I buy water at a convenience store.

vocabulary.notes: コンビニ is a common everyday loanword written in katakana.

vocabulary.title: いくら
vocabulary.notes: いくら asks about an amount or price; it is not written with kanji in this course.

vocabulary.title: 円
vocabulary.notes: 円 follows a number when stating a price in yen.

vocabulary.title: 安い
vocabulary.notes: 安い describes a low price; do not confuse it with the unrelated meaning 'safe' in 安全.

vocabulary.title: 好き

exampleSentences.japanese: 私は日本語が好きです。

vocabulary.notes: 好き normally takes が for the thing that is liked.

vocabulary.title: 欲しい

exampleSentences.japanese: 新しい傘が欲しいです。

vocabulary.notes: 欲しい describes wanting an object; it is different from wanting to do an action.

vocabulary.title: これ
vocabulary.notes: これ refers to something near the speaker; use この before a noun.

vocabulary.title: それ
vocabulary.notes: それ refers to something near the listener or already mentioned.

vocabulary.title: どこ
vocabulary.notes: どこ asks about a place; ここ and そこ answer with near/far-from-speaker locations.

vocabulary.title: 部屋

exampleSentences.translation: There is a desk in the room.

vocabulary.notes: 部屋 is a room inside a building; use に for where something exists.

vocabulary.title: 椅子

exampleSentences.japanese: 机の前に椅子があります。
exampleSentences.translation: There is a chair in front of the desk.

vocabulary.notes: 椅子 is commonly paired with 座る, to sit.

vocabulary.title: 机

exampleSentences.japanese: 机の上に本があります。
exampleSentences.translation: There is a book on the desk.

vocabulary.notes: 机 usually means a desk or study table, not a dining table.

vocabulary.title: 店

exampleSentences.translation: I buy an umbrella at the shop.

vocabulary.notes: 店 is the general word for a shop or store.

vocabulary.title: 前

exampleSentences.translation: I meet in front of the station.

vocabulary.notes: 前 can describe physical position or an earlier time.

vocabulary.title: 上

exampleSentences.japanese: 机の上に本があります。
exampleSentences.translation: There is a book on the desk.

vocabulary.notes: With の, 上の means 'on top of' or 'above' the following noun.

vocabulary.title: 下

exampleSentences.japanese: 机の下に椅子があります。
exampleSentences.translation: There is a chair under the desk.

vocabulary.notes: 下 describes a lower position and often follows の in location phrases.

vocabulary.title: 中

exampleSentences.japanese: 部屋の中に机があります。
exampleSentences.translation: There is a desk inside the room.

vocabulary.notes: 中 means inside or middle depending on the surrounding noun.

vocabulary.title: 会社

exampleSentences.translation: The company is in front of the station.

vocabulary.notes: 会社 can refer to a company or its office depending on context.

vocabulary.title: 話す

exampleSentences.japanese: 友達と日本語を話します。
exampleSentences.translation: I speak Japanese with a friend.

vocabulary.notes: 話す is a godan verb; its polite form is 話します.

vocabulary.title: 週末

exampleSentences.japanese: 週末に友達と会います。
exampleSentences.translation: I meet a friend on the weekend.

vocabulary.notes: 週末 refers to the end of the week, usually Saturday and Sunday.

vocabulary.title: バス

exampleSentences.japanese: バスで学校へ行きます。
exampleSentences.translation: I go to school by bus.

vocabulary.notes: で marks the means of transport in バスで行きます.

vocabulary.title: 時間
vocabulary.notes: 時間 can mean an amount of time or available time depending on context.

vocabulary.title: 図書館

exampleSentences.japanese: 図書館で本を読みます。
exampleSentences.translation: I read a book at the library.

vocabulary.notes: 図書館 is a useful study and public-information location.

vocabulary.title: 寒い
vocabulary.notes: 寒い describes cold weather or surroundings; 冷たい is used for cold things to the touch.

vocabulary.title: 早い
vocabulary.notes: This course uses 早い for early; 速い is the similar-sounding word for fast.

vocabulary.title: 簡単
vocabulary.notes: Use 簡単な before a noun and 簡単です at the end of a polite sentence.

vocabulary.title: 面白い
vocabulary.notes: 面白い can mean interesting or funny; context supplies the nuance.

vocabulary.title: 高い
vocabulary.notes: 高い can describe price or physical height; context decides which meaning fits.

grammar.title: です
grammar.meaning: to state what something is
grammar.formation: Noun + は + Noun/adjective + です
grammar.intuition: です closes a polite statement and lets the listener know how you identify the topic.
usageConditions: Use it for polite present statements.
It can follow a noun or an adjective predicate.
commonMistakes: Do not add です after a polite verb such as 行きます.
The topic marker は is written は but pronounced wa.

grammar.title: は
grammar.meaning: as for X
grammar.formation: Noun + は + information about that noun
grammar.intuition: は puts a small spotlight on the thing you want the rest of the sentence to describe.
usageConditions: Use it to establish or contrast a topic.
It does not always mark the grammatical subject.

examples.translation: As for me, I am a university student.
In the morning, I drink water.

commonMistakes: Do not read は as ha when it is a particle.
Avoid treating は as a universal translation for 'is'.

grammar.title: か
grammar.meaning: turns a polite statement into a question
grammar.formation: Polite sentence + か
grammar.intuition: か at the end opens the sentence for an answer without changing the word order.
usageConditions: Use it at the end of a polite question.
A rising voice is optional in careful speech.
commonMistakes: Do not add English-style do/does words.
Keep the polite ending before か: 行きますか, not 行くですか.

grammar.title: に
grammar.meaning: marks a destination, a specific time, or an existence location
grammar.formation: Destination/time + に + movement or time-sensitive predicate
grammar.intuition: に marks a point the action is aimed at or anchored to.
usageConditions: Use it for a destination with 行く, 来る, and 帰る.
Use it for a clock time or a specific date.
Do not use it for the place where an action happens; use で there.

examples.translation: A friend comes to my home.

commonMistakes: 駅に待ちます is wrong for waiting at a station; say 駅で待ちます.
Recurring time words such as 毎日 usually do not take に.

grammar.title: ます
grammar.meaning: polite non-past action or habit
grammar.formation: Remove the dictionary-form ending and add the polite stem ending: 食べます, 飲みます, 行きます
grammar.intuition: ます gives an action a respectful, everyday conversational finish.
usageConditions: Use it for present habits and future actions when context supplies the time.
Its negative is ません and past is ました.

examples.translation: I will go to the station tomorrow.

commonMistakes: Do not attach ます directly to a dictionary form: 食べるます is wrong.
来ます is pronounced きます, not くます.

grammar.title: ません
grammar.meaning: polite non-past negative
grammar.formation: Replace ます with ません: 食べません, 行きません
grammar.intuition: ません keeps the polite tone while turning an action off.
usageConditions: Use it for things you do not do or will not do.
The time comes from context, just like with ます.

examples.japanese: 今日は学校へ行きません。
examples.translation: I am not going to school today.

commonMistakes: Do not use ないです in this polite verb pattern.
Keep the verb stem before ません: 飲みません, not 飲むません.

grammar.title: ました
grammar.meaning: polite past action
grammar.formation: Replace ます with ました: 食べました, 行きました
grammar.intuition: ました closes a polite action that is already finished.
usageConditions: Use it for completed actions in the past.
A time word such as 昨日 or 先週 makes the time clear.

examples.japanese: 友達と大学へ行きました。
examples.translation: I went to university with a friend.

commonMistakes: Do not use ます for a finished action when the time is clearly past.
The negative past form comes later; do not attach ませんでした yet.

grammar.title: 好きです
grammar.meaning: to like or be fond of N
grammar.formation: Thing liked + が + 好きです
grammar.intuition: 好き describes a positive feeling toward something; が points to what receives that feeling.
usageConditions: Use が for the thing you like in a simple preference statement.
Use 嫌いです for a dislike.

examples.japanese: 私は日本語が好きです。
友達は音楽が好きです。

commonMistakes: Do not automatically use を with 好き; the preferred thing usually takes が.
好き is a な-adjective, so use 好きな before a noun.

grammar.title: 欲しいです
grammar.pattern: N が 欲しいです
grammar.meaning: to want N
grammar.formation: Desired thing + が + 欲しいです
grammar.intuition: 欲しい describes a desire for an object, not an action.
usageConditions: Use が for the thing you want.
Use 〜たい for wanting to do an action; that pattern comes later.

examples.japanese: 新しい傘が欲しいです。

commonMistakes: Do not use を for the object wanted in this basic pattern.
欲しい is an adjective; do not conjugate it like a verb.

grammar.title: ください
grammar.meaning: please give me N
grammar.formation: Requested item + を + ください
grammar.intuition: ください turns a named item into a polite, practical request.
usageConditions: Use it when asking for an item in a shop or service setting.
Add ですか when you want to make the request a question.
commonMistakes: The requested item takes を in this pattern.
ください is already polite; do not add です after it.

grammar.title: あります
grammar.pattern: Place に thing があります
grammar.meaning: there is a non-living thing at a place
grammar.formation: Place + に + thing + が + あります
grammar.intuition: に marks where something exists, while が introduces the thing that is there.
usageConditions: Use あります for objects and places.
Use います for people and animals; that contrast comes next.

examples.japanese: 机の上に本があります。
examples.translation: There is a book on the desk.

examples.japanese: 駅にコンビニがあります。
examples.translation: There is a convenience store at the station.

commonMistakes: Do not use で for the location of existence.
Do not use あります for a person or animal.

grammar.title: を
grammar.meaning: marks the direct object of an action
grammar.formation: Object + を + transitive verb
grammar.intuition: を points to the thing receiving the action.
usageConditions: Use it with actions such as 食べる, 飲む, 読む, and 買う.
The particle を is pronounced o.
commonMistakes: Do not use は when the sentence needs a direct object.
Read を as o, not wo, in modern pronunciation.

grammar.title: で
grammar.meaning: marks where an action happens or what is used to do it
grammar.formation: Place or means + で + action
grammar.intuition: で frames the setting or tool of an action.
usageConditions: Use it for the place where an action happens.
Use it for a means of transport or tool.

examples.japanese: 電車で大学へ行きます。
examples.translation: I go to university by train.

commonMistakes: Use に for a destination, not the place where an action happens.
Use あります with に for existence, not で.

grammar.title: と
grammar.meaning: with a person or together with
grammar.formation: Person + と + shared action
grammar.intuition: と links the person who shares the action with you.
usageConditions: Use it when doing something together with someone.
It can also join nouns in a complete list.

examples.japanese: 家族と大学へ行きます。
examples.translation: I go to university with my family.

commonMistakes: Do not use で for the person you do an action with.
と is different from も, which means also.

grammar.title: の
grammar.meaning: connects a possessor, category, or description to a noun
grammar.formation: Related noun + の + main noun
grammar.intuition: の ties two nouns together so the second one is understood through the first.
usageConditions: Use it for possession, such as 私の本.
Use it for categories or relationships, such as 大学の先生.

examples.japanese: 駅の前に店があります。
examples.translation: There is a shop in front of the station.

commonMistakes: The main noun comes after の.
Do not translate every の as English 'of'; possession is only one use.

grammar.title: も
grammar.meaning: also or too
grammar.formation: N + も + the same predicate
grammar.intuition: も adds another item to an already established statement.
usageConditions: Use it when the new subject or object shares the same information.
も often replaces は, が, or を in simple sentences.

examples.japanese: 友達もこの本を読みます。
examples.translation: My friend also reads this book.

commonMistakes: Do not stack も with は in this basic pattern.
The repeated information can remain understood rather than being said twice.

grammar.title: これ・それ・あれ
grammar.pattern: これ / それ / あれ は N です
grammar.meaning: identifies an object by its distance from the speaker and listener
grammar.formation: これ, それ, or あれ + は + noun + です
grammar.intuition: The demonstrative chooses the viewpoint before you name the thing.
usageConditions: Use これ for something near the speaker.
Use それ for something near the listener or just mentioned; use あれ for something far from both.
commonMistakes: Use この, その, and あの directly before a noun: この本.
Do not use これ本; これ stands alone.

grammar.title: どこですか
grammar.pattern: N は どこですか
grammar.meaning: asks where something or someone is
grammar.formation: Topic + は + どこですか
grammar.intuition: どこ leaves the place slot open for the listener to fill.
usageConditions: Use it to ask for a location.
Use どこへ or どこに with movement verbs when asking about a destination.
commonMistakes: Use どこ for places, not 何 for things.
Keep the question particle か when using a polite question.

grammar.title: います
grammar.pattern: Place に person が います
grammar.meaning: there is a person or animal at a place
grammar.formation: Place + に + living thing + が + います
grammar.intuition: います gives a living presence a place in the scene.
usageConditions: Use it for people and animals.
Use あります for objects and places.

examples.translation: There is a friend in the room.
There is a teacher at school.

commonMistakes: Do not use あります for a person or animal.
The place takes に in an existence sentence.

grammar.title: い-adjectives
grammar.pattern: い-adjective です / くないです / かったです
grammar.meaning: describes qualities in present and past forms
grammar.formation: Keep い for non-past; change い to くない for negative and かった for past.
grammar.intuition: The adjective ending carries the time and polarity of the description.
usageConditions: Use い-adjectives directly before nouns.
For polite predicates, use です after the adjective form.

examples.japanese: 昨日は寒くなかったです。

commonMistakes: Do not add な after an い-adjective before a noun: 寒い日.
Do not say 寒いくない; change い to くない.

grammar.title: Dictionary form
grammar.meaning: the plain non-past form used in basic references and casual statements
grammar.formation: Use the dictionary form such as 食べる, 行く, or 話す.
grammar.intuition: The dictionary form is the compact base form from which many patterns grow.
usageConditions: Use it in dictionaries and casual speech.
Use it before some grammar patterns, including たい and こと.

examples.translation: I go to the library on weekends.

commonMistakes: Do not attach です directly to a plain verb: 行くです.
Do not confuse a dictionary form with the polite ます form.

grammar.title: て-form
grammar.meaning: connects actions in sequence or a related description
grammar.formation: Use a verb's て-form before the next action; common forms include 読んで and 起きて.
grammar.intuition: て-form leaves the sentence open so the next action can follow naturally.
usageConditions: Use it to show actions happening in sequence.
It also appears in permission, prohibition, and requests; those patterns are introduced separately.

examples.japanese: 本を読んで、勉強します。
examples.translation: I read a book and then study.

examples.japanese: 朝起きて、水を飲みます。
examples.translation: I wake up in the morning and drink water.

commonMistakes: Do not use the dictionary form to connect these actions in this pattern.
The て-form of 飲む is 飲んで, not 飲て.

grammar.title: 〜たいです
grammar.meaning: wants to do an action
grammar.formation: Replace ます with たいです: 行きたいです, 読みたいです.
grammar.intuition: たい turns an action into a personal wish or plan.
usageConditions: Use it for wanting to do something.
Use 欲しい for wanting an object.

examples.japanese: 日本語を勉強したいです。
週末に本を読みたいです。
examples.translation: I want to read a book on the weekend.

commonMistakes: Use たい for an action, not for an object you want to own.
Keep the object particle を before the action: 本を読みたいです.

grammar.title: Counters
grammar.meaning: counts people and objects with an appropriate counter
grammar.formation: Place the counter after the number: 三冊 for three books, 二人 for two people.
grammar.intuition: Japanese counts different kinds of things with small category labels.
usageConditions: Use 冊 for bound books and 二人 for two people.
Counter readings can change with certain numbers, so learn useful chunks in context.
commonMistakes: Do not leave a counted noun without a counter in these basic patterns.
Learn the counter reading as a whole phrase rather than translating number by number.

grammar.title: より
grammar.pattern: A は B より adjective です
grammar.meaning: compares A with B
grammar.formation: A + は + B + より + adjective + です
grammar.intuition: より sets the reference point for the comparison.
usageConditions: Use it when saying one thing is more or less a quality than another.
The adjective describes the first item, A.

examples.japanese: 電車はバスより大きいです。
examples.translation: The train is bigger than the bus.

examples.japanese: この本はあの本より面白いです。
examples.translation: This book is more interesting than that book.

commonMistakes: Put the reference item before より.
Do not use と to make this basic comparison.

grammar.title: から
grammar.meaning: because or so
grammar.formation: State the reason + から, then the result or decision.
grammar.intuition: から lets the listener know why the next statement follows.
usageConditions: Use it to give a simple reason for an action or condition.
In beginner polite speech, place から after the polite statement.

examples.japanese: 雨ですから、家にいます。
examples.translation: Because it is raining, I will stay home.

examples.japanese: 時間がありますから、勉強します。
examples.translation: Because I have time, I will study.

commonMistakes: The reason comes before から in these examples.
Do not confuse the reason marker から with the starting-point meaning of から.

grammar.title: てもいいですか
grammar.meaning: asks for permission to do something
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + もいいですか
grammar.intuition: もいいですか checks whether an action is acceptable.
usageConditions: Use it politely before doing an action.
A positive answer can be いいですよ; a refusal may use いけません.

examples.japanese: ここで話してもいいですか。
この本を見てもいいですか。
examples.translation: May I look at this book?

commonMistakes: Keep も in the pattern: 話してもいいですか.
Use the て-form before もいい, not the dictionary form.

grammarContrasts.title: は and が
grammarContrasts.explanation: At this stage, use は to introduce the topic you want to talk about. が more narrowly identifies the subject or answers 'who/what' is involved. They can overlap in simple sentences, but they do not create the same focus.

examples.translation: As for me, I am a student.

examples.japanese: 誰が学生ですか。私が学生です。
examples.translation: Who is a student? I am the student.

exercises: Choose は when the sentence is setting a topic.
Choose が when the sentence answers who or what did it.

grammarContrasts.title: に and で
grammarContrasts.explanation: に marks a destination or a point in time. で marks the place or means where an action happens. Ask whether the sentence points toward a place or describes activity inside it.

examples.translation: I wait for the train at the station.

exercises: Fill the destination: 大学___行きます。
Fill the action location: 家___勉強します。

grammarContrasts.title: ます, ません, and ました
grammarContrasts.explanation: The stem stays the same while the ending tells the listener whether the polite action is non-past, negative, or finished in the past.

examples.translation: I read a book every day.

exercises: Change the action to a polite negative: 飲みます → 飲みません。
Choose the finished action: 行きます or 行きました。

grammarContrasts.title: 好き and 欲しい
grammarContrasts.explanation: 好き describes a positive feeling toward something. 欲しい describes wanting to have an object. Both commonly use が, but they answer different questions.

examples.japanese: 新しい本が欲しいです。

exercises: Use 好き for a preference and 欲しい for a desired object.
Ask what someone wants: 何が欲しいですか。

grammarContrasts.title: を and で
grammarContrasts.explanation: を marks the thing receiving an action. で marks where the action happens or the means used to do it.
exercises: Choose を for the object: 水___飲みます。
Choose で for the setting: 部屋___勉強します。

grammarContrasts.title: の and も
grammarContrasts.explanation: の connects nouns. も adds another noun to the same statement as 'also' or 'too'.

examples.translation: My friend is also a student.

exercises: Connect the nouns: 大学___先生。
Add 'also': 私___学生です。

grammarContrasts.title: これ and どこ
grammarContrasts.explanation: これ identifies a nearby object. どこ asks for a place. They both help you navigate a simple conversation without needing a long description.
exercises: Use これ when pointing at an object.
Use どこ when asking for a location.

grammarContrasts.title: あります and います
grammarContrasts.explanation: あります describes non-living things. います describes people and animals. Both use に for the place where something exists.
exercises: Use あります for an object.
Use います for a person or animal.

grammarContrasts.title: い-adjective forms
grammarContrasts.explanation: い-adjectives change their ending to express a negative or past description, while keeping the adjective meaning visible.

examples.japanese: 昨日は寒くなかったです。

exercises: Change 寒い to its negative form: 寒くないです。
Choose the past form: 面白かったです。

grammarContrasts.title: Dictionary form and ます form
grammarContrasts.explanation: The dictionary form is a plain base form. The ます form expresses the same action in a polite register.
exercises: Match 読む with its polite form 読みます.
Do not attach です directly to 行く.

grammarContrasts.title: て-form and たい
grammarContrasts.explanation: て-form connects an action to what follows. たい changes an action into a desire, so the two forms do different jobs.

examples.japanese: 本を読んで、勉強します。
examples.translation: I read a book and then study.
I want to read a book.

exercises: Use て-form to connect two actions.
Use たい to say you want to do an action.

readings.title: 朝の駅
readings.passage: 毎朝、私は七時に起きます。水を飲んで、駅へ行きます。駅で友達を待ちます。友達と電車で大学へ行きます。
readings.translation: Every morning, I wake up at seven. I drink water and go to the station. I wait for a friend at the station. I go to university by train with my friend.

questions.prompt: 毎朝、何時に起きますか。
questions.explanation: 毎朝、私は七時に起きます。

questions.prompt: 友達と何で大学へ行きますか。
questions.explanation: 友達と電車で大学へ行きます。

readings.title: 家の昼ご飯
readings.passage: 今日は学校へ行きません。家で昼ご飯を食べます。水を飲んで、本を読みます。午後、大学へ行きます。
readings.translation: Today I am not going to school. I eat lunch at home. I drink water and read a book. In the afternoon, I go to university.

questions.prompt: 今日はどこで昼ご飯を食べますか。
questions.explanation: 家で昼ご飯を食べます。

questions.prompt: 午後、どこへ行きますか。

readings.title: 新しい本
readings.passage: これは新しい本です。大学の本です。大きい本ですが、読みやすいです。友達もこの本を読みます。
readings.translation: This is a new book. It is a university book. It is a big book, but it is easy to read. My friend also reads this book.

questions.prompt: この本はどんな本ですか。
questions.explanation: これは新しい本です。大きい本ですが、読みやすいです。

questions.prompt: だれがこの本を読みますか。
questions.explanation: 友達もこの本を読みます。

readings.title: 雨の日の買い物
readings.passage: 今日は雨です。私はコンビニへ行きます。水と傘を買います。傘は五百円です。
readings.translation: It is raining today. I go to a convenience store. I buy water and an umbrella. The umbrella is 500 yen.

questions.prompt: 今日はどんな天気ですか。
傘はいくらですか。

readings.title: 私の部屋
readings.passage: これは私の部屋です。部屋の中に机と椅子があります。机の上に本があります。机の下には何もありません。
readings.translation: This is my room. There is a desk and a chair inside the room. There is a book on the desk. There is nothing under the desk.

questions.prompt: 部屋の中に何がありますか。
questions.explanation: 部屋の中に机と椅子があります。

questions.prompt: 本はどこにありますか。
questions.explanation: 机の上に本があります。

readings.title: 忙しい日
readings.passage: 今日は寒いです。私は図書館へ行きます。図書館で本を二冊読みます。週末は友達と本を読みたいです。
readings.translation: Today is cold. I go to the library. I read two books at the library. On the weekend, I want to read books with a friend.

questions.prompt: 今日はどんな天気ですか。
週末、だれと本を読みたいですか。
questions.explanation: 週末は友達と本を読みたいです。

listening.title: 駅で会いましょう
listening.situation: Two friends arrange where to meet before going to university.
listening.transcript:
A: 明日、何時に駅へ来ますか。
B: 七時に来ます。駅の前で会いましょう。
A: はい、わかりました。

questions.prompt: 二人は何時に会いますか。
二人はどこで会いますか。
questions.explanation: 駅の前で会いましょう。

listening.title: 水をください
listening.situation: A customer orders a meal and a drink.
listening.transcript:
A: いらっしゃいませ。何にしますか。
B: ご飯にします。水もお願いします。
A: はい、わかりました。

questions.prompt: お客さんは何を食べますか。
お客さんは何と言って飲み物を頼みますか。

listening.title: 夜の予定
listening.situation: Two friends talk about what one will do in the evening.
listening.transcript:
A: 夜、何をしますか。
B: 家で本を読みます。それから、勉強します。
A: そうですか。

questions.prompt: 夜、どこで本を読みますか。
本を読んだあと、何をしますか。

listening.title: 傘を買います
listening.situation: A customer asks the price of an umbrella and decides to buy it.
listening.transcript:
A: この傘はいくらですか。
B: 五百円です。
A: では、この傘をください。

questions.prompt: 傘はいくらですか。
お客さんは何を買いますか。

listening.title: 駅はどこですか
listening.situation: A visitor asks where the station is and receives a simple direction.
listening.transcript:
A: すみません。駅はどこですか。
B: あの店の前です。
A: ありがとうございます。

questions.prompt: 駅はどこですか。
Aさんは何と言いましたか。
answers: ありがとうございます
questions.explanation: ありがとうございます。

listening.title: 週末の予定
listening.situation: Two friends talk about a weekend plan at the library.
listening.transcript:
A: 週末、何をしたいですか。
B: 図書館で本を読みたいです。
A: 何冊読みますか。
B: 二冊読みます。

questions.prompt: 週末、何をしたいですか。
answers: 図書館で本を読みたいです
questions.explanation: 図書館で本を読みたいです。

questions.prompt: 何冊読みますか。
